title: Security review: SSO/SCIM & RBAC for ZenHealth
meeting_header: Date: 2026-07-02 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~50 mins | Attendees: Jamie Coleman (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood CSM); Laura Chen (ZenHealth CTO), Marcus Reed (ZenHealth SecEng), Anita Gomez (ZenHealth IT), Tom Ellis (ZenHealth Compliance)
summary: Redwood walkthrough of SSO (SAML) and SCIM onboarding plus RBAC/least-privilege model. Discussed SAML metadata exchange, SCIM provisioning options, group sync, mapping to Redwood roles, audit logging, KMS/encryption, data residency, SOC 2 artifacts. Agreed next steps: share SAML metadata, send SCIM config guide, provide role matrix template and SOC2/ISO reports; schedule pilot in 2 weeks.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call... we got Laura, Marcus, Anita, Tom from ZenHealth; Ravi and I from Redwood, and Sofia from CS. How's everyone?
[00:10] Laura (ZenHealth - CTO): Doing well, thanks. We'll try to keep this focused; main thing is SSO/SCIM and making sure RBAC meets our least-privilege needs.
[00:20] Ravi (Redwood SE): Great, I'll drive the technical bits — we'll go through SAML metadata flow, SCIM provisioning, and our RBAC model. Happy to answer any compliance questions too.
[00:28] Marcus (ZenHealth - SecEng): Quick callout — we require SAML with signed assertions, SCIM v2 for automated provisioning, and everything must support our KMS for encryption keys. Also we have strict data residency requirements in eu-west-1 for certain PII.
[00:40] Jamie: Noted. We'll flag that. Redwood supports SAML with signed assertions, we can host the IdP or integrate with your Okta. SCIM v2 is supported — group sync and deprovisioning included. For KMS, we have integrations for customer-managed keys in our Private deployment; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with AWS KMS, and dedicated customers can bring keys.
[01:05] Anita (ZenHealth - IT Ops): If you say "hosted" here, what does that mean for audit logs? We need 1 year retention and exportable logs for audits.
[01:13] Sofia (Redwood CSM): We have configurable audit log retention tiers — we can retain logs for 1 year on hosted with the premium observability add-on, and we can deliver logs to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch/Logstash) via streaming. We'll share the export playbook.
[01:30] Tom (ZenHealth - Compliance): Also need SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence. Do you have attestation we can share with our compliance folks?
[01:38] Jamie: Yes, we will attach current SOC 2 and ISO reports under NDA. I'll put that in the follow-up email.
[01:45] [00:55] Ravi: Okay, diving into SAML. Typical flow: we exchange metadata, you configure Redwood as a service provider in Okta/AzureAD, we provide ACS and entity ID. We support signed authn requests and enforce NameID format options. A couple of customers use email as NameID, others use persistent IDs — whichever you prefer.
[02:10] Marcus: We prefer transient or persistent? We have to avoid email as a stable identifier because of rotation rules. Persistent is fine. Also we require signed assertions and want the ability to limit session length.
[02:20] Ravi: Persistent + signed assertions + configurable session timeout is supported. Our default session TTL is 8 hours but you can set 1h or down to 15m per your policy.
[02:30] Laura: For SCIM — we need group-based provisioning that maps to roles in Redwood, and automatic deprovisioning on user removal. Do you support groups from Okta?
[02:38] Ravi: Yes, SCIM v2 supports group membership sync. We map SCIM groups to Redwood roles via a role-mapping table. We'll show the mapping UI and also the API-first option if you want to script it.
[02:50] [03:00] Jamie: On RBAC, our recommended least-privilege model has three primary roles for your org: Admin (full control), Developer (create routes, view logs but no billing), and Viewer (read-only). We also support custom roles and fine-grained permissions — e.g., grant route-level deploy rights, or token creation bounds.
[03:15] Marcus: We need separation of duties: security folks cannot create billing policies, and devs shouldn't be able to alter audit settings. Can you lock certain permissions behind SAML group membership and only let SSO users in a security group get those permissions?
[03:25] Ravi: Absolutely — role assignment can be group-based. You can map Okta groups like znh-admins, znh-devs, znh-sec to Redwood roles. We also support SCIM-based dynamic group updates so changes propagate.
[03:38] Anita: What about service accounts for CI/CD? They should not be interactive users.
[03:43] Sofia: We support machine tokens / service accounts with scoped permissions and expiry. They can be provisioned through the API and tied to projects; you can restrict them to certain models or routes.
[03:55] Tom: Audit logs — how granular are they? We need to see who rotated keys, who changed RBAC, who pushed model updates, and be able to export them for forensic reviews.
[04:05] Ravi: Our audit logs include user identity (SAML subject), action, resource, timestamp, and IP. We log admin actions like key rotations, role changes, model rollouts, and token creation. Logs are immutable and can be forwarded to your log storage.
[04:20] Marcus: Are logs tamper-evident? We need to prove integrity.
[04:23] Jamie: We support append-only logs with checksum and can include Radix or HMAC signatures on batches when exporting, and we can also provide Hash-based verification metadata. We'll include details in the tech pack.
[04:38] [04:50] Marcus: Encryption at rest — if we go hosted we'd like CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys). Is that possible?
[04:55] Ravi: For our hosted API we offer envelope encryption with our provider KMS by default; CMEK is available for Redwood Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers willing to sign an addendum and meet certain requirements, we can also enable bring-your-own-key for sensitive classes. We'll flag legal here.
[05:15] Laura: Data residency — some PHI must remain in eu-west-1. Can you pin workload and storage region?
[05:22] Ravi: Yes, you can pin models and storage to eu-west-1 in Dedicated or in our Private VPC. For hosted, we have region controls and can ensure requests and logs are stored in eu-west-1 for specific projects, but full guarantees require Dedicated.
[05:35] Anita: Does the SCIM sync push PII? We want just usernames and group membership; no email content or profile pictures.
[05:42] Ravi: SCIM payload can be scoped — we only require userName, externalId (optional), active flag, and groups. We do not fetch passwords or profile pictures. We'll share the exact attribute map.
[05:55] [06:10] Jamie: A few real-world caveats we usually cover: 1) SCIM sync timing — it's near real-time but group membership changes can take a couple minutes. 2) Deprovisioning: we can soft-delete and then hard-delete after retention window. 3) If you want SAML Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning, we support that too but recommend SCIM for enterprise scale.
[06:35] Marcus: For JIT, what's the identifier used?
[06:38] Ravi: We accept NameID persistent and map it to userName in Redwood. If SCIM exists, SCIM authoritative wins for group membership.
[06:45] Laura: We want RBAC audit trail tied to user IDs not emails. Are SAML subjects stable?
[06:50] Ravi: Use persistent NameID or externalId from SCIM so the user ID is stable across email changes. We'll show configuration to use externalId as primary key.
[07:00] [07:20] Tom: Can we do attribute-based access control (ABAC) or just role-based?
[07:25] Ravi: Currently mostly RBAC with fine-grained roles and resource scoping; we have attribute tags on resources (projects, environments) and you can combine role + project scope. Full ABAC is on our roadmap, timeline TBD.
[07:40] Anita: Onboarding flow — what's the minimum lead time to enable SSO+SCIM for our 250 users?
[07:45] Sofia: Typical timeline is 2-3 business days for SAML metadata exchange and config, another 3-5 days for SCIM pilot with a few groups, and then a week for org-wide sync and audits. So plan ~2 weeks for pilot end-to-end.
[08:00] Jamie: For compliance pack, we'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, and our pen test summary under NDA. We'll also provide the SAML metadata, SCIM config guide, and a role mapping template.
[08:12] Marcus: About pen tests — do you allow us to run a limited external scan?
[08:16] Jamie: Yes, scheduled and scoped tests are OK with notice; there is a sign-up form. We'll share the process.
[08:25] [08:35] Customer question (unattributed): How do you handle emergency access / break-glass?
[08:40] Ravi: We support emergency admin access with MFA and rationale capture; that action is logged with elevated retention. We also have an approval flow.
[08:50] Laura: One more — do you support SCIM delta syncs and pagination? Our directory is large.
[08:55] Ravi: Yes, we support SCIM delta syncs, bulk operations, and pagination. Throughput is configurable and we can throttle to match your IdP.
[09:05] [09:15] Jamie: Any blockers or hard requirements we haven't covered?
[09:18] Marcus: We need signed SAML assertions, SCIM v2 with group sync and deprovisioning, CMEK or guaranteed region residency for PHI, audit logs export to our SIEM, and SOC2/ISO reports. That's basically it.
[09:30] Jamie: All feasible. Action items captured and we'll follow-up.
[09:35] [09:45] Sofia: Next steps — I'll set up a pilot workspace in eu-west-1, share SCIM guide, role template, and SOC pack. Can we target the week of July 20th for pilot?
[09:55] Laura: That works.
[10:00] Jamie: Great. Thanks everyone. We will send the email with attachments and schedule the kickoff.
[10:08] [End of recording]
